g.style: font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 14; line-height: 1.7; fill: #3a3a5a;
g.text: Japan (Nihon/Nippon) is an island nation in East Asia, comprising four main islands — Hokkaido, Honshu, Shikoku, and Kyushu — plus thousands of smaller islands.
With a population of ~124 million (2024), it ranks 11th globally. The Greater Tokyo Area is the world's most populous metropolitan area at 37.4 million.

A constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary government, Japan is a G7 member and the world's 4th-largest economy by nominal GDP. It leads in robotics, automotive, electronics, and cultural exports.
The country balances deep tradition — Shinto shrines, tea ceremony, seasonal festivals — with cutting-edge modernity, from neon-lit megacities to high-speed Shinkansen.

g.style: font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 15; line-height: 1.7; fill: #3a3a5a;
g.text: Why Japan matters: As the world's fourth-largest economy and a linchpin of Indo-Pacific security, Japan combines technological leadership with soft-power influence through anime, cuisine, design, and tourism. Its aging society (29% over 65) drives innovation in robotics and healthcare, while its commitment to carbon neutrality by 2050 shapes global energy markets. For travelers, Japan offers unmatched contrasts — ancient temples beside neon districts, alpine wilderness beside subtropical beaches — all connected by the world's most punctual rail network.

g.style: font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 14; line-height: 1.7; fill: #3a3a5a;
g.text: Japan's nominal GDP in current US dollars peaked at $5.12T (2019) before the pandemic and yen depreciation reversed gains. The 2024 figure of $4.03T reflects a weaker yen (¥150+/USD) rather than real output decline.

Key drivers: automotive (Toyota, Honda), semiconductors (equipment, materials), robotics, and cultural exports. The Bank of Japan's policy shift in 2024 — ending negative rates — signals a new macroeconomic phase.
Real GDP growth has been modest (~0.5–1.0% annually), but GDP per capita (PPP) remains high at ~$52k. Corporate governance reforms (Tokyo Stock Exchange pressure) are improving shareholder returns.
Note: Japanese government does not census ethnicity; figures based on nationality/residency. "Japanese" includes naturalized citizens.
